title: introduce-stateful-controlplane-sg-templates-and-peering-lifecycle-hooks
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: customers deploying the private control plane have asked for deterministic, AZ-aware outbound egress controls, safer peering lifecycle handling across accounts, and explicit DNS forwarding validation so upgrades don't silently break service discovery. This PR adds stateful security-group templates for control-plane instances and pods (per-AZ naming and tags), introduces installer-managed peering lifecycle hooks to avoid stale peer routes during rolling upgrades, and adds a DNS TTL sanity check/opt-in forwarding policy. What changed: 1) terraform/modules/controlplane: new module 'sg_templates' that generates stateful SGs with deterministic names, per-az egress ip-pools annotation support, and KMS-encrypted tag metadata. 2) installer/hooks/peering-lifecycle: a small shell+py hook that runs after VPC create to accept peering across accounts when cross-account role is provided, and that performs safe teardown ordering during destroy. 3) helm/controlplane/values.yaml: new values.controlPlane.egress.policy and values.controlPlane.egress.azIpPools to enable AZ isolated egress. 4) terraform/roles: optional cross-account role and readme describing minimal IAM. 5) infra/route-policy: small module to toggle route propagation and attach deterministic route tables to controlplane subnets. 6) docs/upgrade-playbook.md: rollout guidance, canary checklist, and rollback steps. Checklist: [x] Terraform validate and fmt [x] Unit tests for hook scripts [x] Integration smoke test against minimal private deployment [x] Docs updated Release plan: merge to main, cut a private-installer release, stage to qa cluster with --set controlPlane.egress.policy=az-isolated then promote to staging. Backout: change policy to 'shared' and run peering teardown hook which will unroll routes in reverse-order. Usage notes: by default new behavior is opt-in via helm values.controlPlane.egress.policy, existing deployments continue unchanged until operator flips the flag. The peering accepter requires a cross-account role ARN in terraform/roles/README when peering across org boundaries. Quick example snippet: terraform module "controlplane" { source = "./modules/controlplane" control_plane_subnets = var.control_plane_subnets egress_policy = "az-isolated" peering_accepter_role_arn = var.peer_accepter_role_arn }

release_notes: Added stateful, AZ-aware control-plane security group templates (opt-in via helm values)
Installer-managed peering lifecycle hooks to safely create and teardown cross-account VPC peers
Optional cross-account accepter role with example terraform configuration
Route policy toggle for deterministic route table attachment to control-plane subnets
DNS TTL sanity check and conditional Route53 forwarding policy (opt-in)
upgrade_instructions: Default behavior is unchanged; to opt into AZ-isolated egress set helm values.controlPlane.egress.policy=az-isolated and provide values.controlPlane.egress.azIpPools
If peering across accounts, populate terraform var peer_accepter_role_arn with a role that has ec2:AcceptVpcPeeringConnection and logs to the installer S3 bucket
Follow docs/upgrade-playbook.md for canary and rollback steps
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: incorrect SG rules could block egress during rollout. Mitigation: opt-in flag and canary on a subset of AZs; thorough smoke tests included.
Risk: cross-account peering failures due to IAM. Mitigation: explicit README and example role; peering hook will retry and fail-fast with clear logs.
Risk: added hooks increase install time. Mitigation: hooks are async by default and can be gated by operator-run flag.
testing_summary: Unit: sg template variable permutations and template linting (tests/unit/test_sg_templates.py)
Integration: peering create/accept/teardown smoke test against ephemeral VPC in CI (tests/integration/test_peering_lifecycle.py)
Manual: deployed to qa private cluster, verified DNS forwarding TTL check and sample control-plane workload egress through AZ IP pools
notes: This PR is intended to be fully opt-in; no automatic migration will occur.
Customers with managed egress or strict audit requirements should consult the new docs before enabling az-isolated mode.
